grades.quote: Irreparable corruption, such as two files using the same block, must be avoided at all costs. Noncritical reparable corruption, such as a lost block, can be repaired whenever convenient. Critical reparable corruption, such as a block that is both in use and “free,” must be repaired before the system returns to normal operation.
grades.reason: Directly explains that a lost block only wastes space, whereas an in-use block marked free risks reallocation to another file and irreparable corruption.
Discusses file-to-storage mapping, not crash-induced metadata inconsistencies or their consequences.
Explains delayed allocation and free-space allocation policies, not lost blocks versus blocks simultaneously in use and marked free.
